quarterly_data.signal: NetApp has outsourced manufacturing operations to third parties located in Fremont and San Jose, California; Laredo, Texas; Guadalajara, Mexico; Helmond, The Netherlands; Tiszaujvaros, Hungary; Taoyuan, Taiwan; and Singapore, using contract manufacturers for major subassemblies and final system configuration, and depends on a limited number of suppliers (some single-source) for drives and other components. The 10-K states NetApp experienced inflationary pressure and supply chain constraints beginning in the second half of fiscal 2026, resulting in increased costs for memory and other components that adversely affected its gross margin.

As of April 24, 2026 NetApp had $1.0 billion in non-cancelable purchase commitments for inventory, i.e. inventory commitments with third-party contract manufacturers and component suppliers made to manage manufacturer lead times, meet product forecasts and purchase key components used in the manufacture of its products. Remaining performance obligations were $5.7 billion as of April 24, 2026, of which 45% is expected to be recognized as revenue in the next 12 months. NetApp paid $198 million for capital expenditures in fiscal 2026 ($168 million in fiscal 2025).
